universal_truth: The Sun is a star, a giant ball of hot gas that gives us light and heat.
The Moon orbits Earth and reflects the Sun's light; it doesn't make its own light.
Water covers most of Earth and can exist as ice, liquid, or gas (steam).
Trees breathe in what we breathe out (carbon dioxide) and give us fresh air (oxygen).
Gravity is the invisible force that pulls everything down toward the center of the Earth.
Earth has seasons because it is tilted as it travels around the Sun.
Clouds are made of tiny water droplets or ice crystals floating in the sky.
Wind is just air moving from one place to another because of changes in temperature.
Stars are far-away suns that look tiny because they are trillions of miles away.
Planets are large worlds that orbit around a star; Earth is one of eight in our family.
